correctness.rationale: Exact normal-equation coarse correction and Richardson matrices are multiplied directly. Each resulting rank-one matrix has the singular norm given by a closed scalar expression. A nonnegative squared identity bounds the pre-smoothed norm; differentiating a rational function gives the post-smoothed sharp supremum and optimizer; negativity of the cubic below 2 and strict monotonicity above 2 establishes the unique Euclidean safety transition. The common trace and determinant zero imply the exact T^j=λ^{j-1}T power law. 1,510 numerical matrix tests and extremum checks corroborate but do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The same SPD system, strictly contractive Richardson smoother, and identical coarse space can be Euclidean-safe if smoothed before least-squares correction yet amplify the error if smoothed afterward. The exact sharp threshold and linear-in-conditioning amplification quantify a natural finite-horizon design risk hidden by common asymptotic eigenvalue rates. This is a complete natural 2D classification rather than an arbitrary unmotivated sample or normalization check.
